title: Investigate failed gradual rollout due to route-priority mismatch and rollback stuck
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Post-incident follow-up for a failed gradual model rollout on 2026-02-18 where a route-priority mismatch caused A/B routing to direct traffic incorrectly and subsequent rollback attempts became stuck due to version pinning and resource reservation behavior. This ticket collects timeline, root-cause analysis, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: Symptom: 5% canary traffic experienced elevated error rates (502/504) and p90 latency increased from 180ms to 2.3s for ~12 minutes
Scope: ~24 paying customers saw degraded inference; no data loss but degraded availability for canary cohort
Immediate mitigation: manual traffic swipe back to baseline model and emergency scaling of compatible instances; manual fix completed at 2026-02-18 15:07 UTC
timeline: 2026-02-18 14:47 UTC - Automated canary rollout (5% weight) initiated for model v2026-02-a

2026-02-18 14:50 UTC - Control plane applied new route with priority=10 but autoscaler/route reconciler used priority=5 in a subsequent update (race), causing a split routing table where some edges still matched the canary predicate incorrectly
2026-02-18 14:51 UTC - Early errors observed: rapid increase in 502 from backend variant due to KV-cache warmup mismatch and kernel selection fallback - alert fired

2026-02-18 14:53 UTC - Runbook triggered: attempt automated rollback. Rollback plan failed to schedule because the Dedicated pool had several host-level version_pins (customers pinned to v2026-01-x) and resource reservations prevented immediate fallback allocation

2026-02-18 15:00 UTC - Oncall engaged, attempted manual override to drain canary traffic; some regions still reported misrouted requests due to stale routing shards (control plane partially applied change)
2026-02-18 15:07 UTC - Manual global route override completed; traffic returned to baseline. Post-incident triage started.
2026-02-19 10:00 UTC - Initial RCA finished; provisioning of a dedicated debug cluster to replicate mismatch was scheduled (ENG-12850)
2026-02-25 - Observability gaps identified: lack of single view correlating route-priority diffs, instance version_pins, and autoscaler reservations
root_causes: Control plane race while reconciling routing updates led to inconsistent route-priority values across edge shards (priority mismatch), causing A/B predicates to match incorrectly
Rollback automation assumed capacity to spawn compatible fallbacks; however, host-level version_pins and reserved capacity for enterprise customers prevented immediate scheduling
Insufficient preflight checks: rollout validation did not verify deterministic shard convergence nor check for active version pins or reservation constraints before shifting traffic
Observability/alerting did not surface the intersection of routing diffs and resource reservation state as a single correlated alert
action_items: ENG-13001 - Add preflight validator to rollout pipeline that checks: (a) route-priority convergence across edge shards, (b) active version_pins in target pools, and (c) reservation headroom. Owner: Ben Martinez. Due: 2026-03-18

ENG-13002 - Enhance rollback automation to fall back to a compatible model variant in the same pool or to gracefully throttle canary traffic if capacity is constrained. Owner: Rong Liu. Due: 2026-03-25

ENG-13003 - Implement a cross-cutting correlated alert that surfaces simultaneous route diffs + scheduling failures + increased 5xx from canaries. Owner: Priya Shah (Observability). Due: 2026-03-10 (prototype)
ENG-13004 - Remove implicit host-level version_pins or make them visible to rollout planner; add an API to query reservation constraints. Owner: Platform team. Due: 2026-04-01
ENG-13005 - Run a weekly simulation for 2 weeks that performs dry-run rollouts and validates shard convergence and rollback behavior. Owner: Oncall team. Due: 2026-03-30
ENG-13006 - Update runbook run steps to include explicit verification of routing shard convergence and a one-click global-override quick action. Owner: SRE. Due: 2026-03-12
notes: Design review: PM requested a conservative default that requires explicit opt-in for cross-pool fallback due to cost implications
Security: no sensitive data was exposed; KMS/HSM paths unaffected
Customer communications: support sent a summary to affected customers on 2026-02-19; CS asked for a postmortem link and action timeline
Follow-up: evaluate whether canary cohort size should be reduced for cross-pool rollouts until preflight checks are in place
